trigger: CREATE TABLE a(b); SELECT (SELECT b FROM a GROUP BY b HAVING (SELECT COUNT()OVER() + lead(b)OVER(ORDER BY SUM(DISTINCT b)+b))) FROM a UNION SELECT 99 ORDER BY 1;
notes: Two-arm ASAN probe on the pre-fix tree a0365c487c12: with the default lookaside arena ASAN is SILENT; with -lookaside 0 0 it reports heap-use-after-free, 40 bytes inside an 88-byte region, in resetAccumulator - the function NVD names. The dangling object is an Expr held by an AggInfo; Expr comes from sqlite3DbMallocRawNN(db,sizeof(Expr)+nExtra) (src/expr.c:941), 72-88 bytes, far below the 1200-byte lookaside slot.

bug_class: heap-buffer-overflow (write) into the neighbouring arena slot
trigger: IN operator with a vector LHS reached through a RIGHT JOIN subroutine, where the loop's equality-term count is smaller than the vector width (dbsqlfuzz 14cfdad6ca45e607163f54049ddf5065183dc657)
notes: aiMap = sqlite3DbMallocZero(pParse->db, sizeof(int)*nEq) was sized by the equality-term count while sqlite3FindInIndex writes one int per vector term. Instrumented the identical call in the pre-fix tree: aiMap is 8 bytes and lands inside [db->lookaside.pStart, db->lookaside.pEnd) - printed lookaside=YES - so the overflow writes into the adjacent lookaside slot, never past a malloc block. NOT linked to any CVE: no SQLite check-in message mentions one.

trigger: CREATE TABLE v1(v2 UNIQUE, v3 AS(TYPEOF(NULL)) UNIQUE); SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT TRUE) FROM v1 GROUP BY likelihood(v3,0.100000);
notes: sqlite3Select deleted the pDistinct ExprList before sqlite3WhereEnd, which still holds it. Two-arm ASAN probe on pre-fix tree 55938b5fa0cb: SILENT with the arena on; with -lookaside 0 0, heap-use-after-free, a 72-byte WRITE (memcpy) 8 bytes into an 88-byte region, in sqlite3WhereEnd. 88 bytes is a small (128-byte) lookaside slot.

trigger: VALUES(1) INTERSECT SELECT * WINDOW f AS () ORDER BY x COLLATE nocase;
notes: The compound-to-subquery rewrite copied the Select without clearing p->pWinDefn, so two Selects free the same Window list. Two-arm ASAN probe on pre-fix tree 0232dade7977: SILENT with the arena on; with -lookaside 0 0, heap-use-after-free 72 bytes inside a 152-byte region in sqlite3WindowListDelete. Window is 144-152 bytes = a full-size (1200-byte) lookaside slot. Under the arena the second free pushes the same slot onto db->lookaside.pFree twice, so the free list hands one slot to two owners - a type-confusion primitive rather than a crash.

trigger: a window-function query in which the master window's PARTITION BY expression list is deleted with the Window object and then reused by the rewrite
poc: yes - Talos ships one (./sqlite3 -init poc); the SQL itself is not published
notes: The advisory itself walks the free into SQLite's lookaside path, quoting isLookaside(db,p) and the slot-recycling code, and notes the freed slot is only poisoned in debug builds. Affected 3.26.0 and 3.27.0; vendor patched 2019-03-28 per the advisory timeline. fix_commit left empty: no fetched source names a check-in, and the candidate ones are circumstantial.

bug_class: out-of-bounds read (4 bytes past the page buffer)
trigger: corrupt auto-vacuum database whose cell declares a size running past the end of its b-tree page
poc: no single-case file; the maintainer's dbfuzz2/dbsqlfuzz corpora (test/fuzzdata*.db)
notes: get4byte(&pCell[info.nSize-4]) reads past pPage->aDataEnd; the fix adds a SQLITE_WITHIN(pPage->aDataEnd,...) guard. MemPage.aData is a page-cache page buffer. By default pcache1InitBulk (src/pcache1.c:297) carves the first SQLITE_DEFAULT_PCACHE_INITSZ=20 pages of every cache out of ONE sqlite3Malloc block - measured here as a single 87360-byte allocation (20 x 4368) - and each slot is laid out [page buffer | PgHdr1 | extra] (src/pcache1.c:318). SQLite has deliberately placed the header immediately after the page buffer since 2009 so that small overreads stay mapped, which is precisely why an allocator-boundary check cannot see them.

trigger: CREATE VIRTUAL TABLE t0 USING fts3(...); INSERT INTO t0 VALUES('one','1234','aaaa','bbbb'); SELECT snippet(t0) FROM t0 WHERE t0 MATCH '(def AND (one NEAR abc)) OR one';
notes: CONTROL. Two-arm ASAN probe on pre-fix tree c48428899d5b: ASAN reports heap-use-after-free of a 216-byte region in fts3SnippetAdvance in BOTH arms, i.e. with the lookaside arena at its default. FTS3 allocates with sqlite3_realloc64/sqlite3_malloc64 (e.g. ext/fts3/fts3.c:1947), so its frees reach the system allocator and a bounds/revocation scheme sees them.

poc: yes - test/json101.test cases 22.1-22.2, forum post b25edc1d4662
notes: CONTROL. Two-arm ASAN probe on pre-fix tree 66dacae4c3f8: heap-use-after-free of a 96-byte region in jsonParseAddNodeArray in BOTH arms. The node array is grown with sqlite3_realloc64 and released with sqlite3_free, so the cache spill's free reaches the system allocator.

trigger: a self-referential VIEW whose body nests three CTEs, after ALTER TABLE RENAME COLUMN, then SELECT from the view (forum post aa4a7a3980)
notes: CONTROL, and the most instructive one: a 72-byte core parse-tree object (With) that is NOT arena memory. Two-arm ASAN probe on pre-fix tree acef1abda274: heap-use-after-free in searchWith in BOTH arms. Full allocation stack shows sqlite3DbMallocZero -> dbMallocRawFinish -> sqlite3Malloc, from withDup <- sqlite3SelectDup <- sqlite3ViewGetColumnNames, which runs inside a DisableLookaside region (src/build.c:3154). Ruled out pool exhaustion by rerunning with -lookaside 1200 4000: still system malloc. Size alone does not decide arena residency.

trigger: PRAGMA writable_schema=1; then rewrite the sqlite_sequence row in sqlite_schema to a malformed CREATE TABLE, reopen, and INSERT into the AUTOINCREMENT table
notes: CONTROL. Two-arm ASAN probe on pre-fix tree f22c590bab1a: heap-use-after-free 72 bytes inside a 128-byte region in autoIncBegin in BOTH arms. Allocation stack: sqlite3StartTable -> sqlite3DbMallocZero -> dbMallocRawFinish. Reason: the grammar rule createkw ::= CREATE calls disableLookaside(pParse) (src/parse.y:211-213), so every CREATE statement parses with the arena off and all schema objects (Table, Index, Trigger) are ordinary heap.

trigger: CREATE VIRTUAL TABLE ft USING fts3; INSERT rows; UPDATE ft_segdir SET root = X'...FFFFFFFF...'; SELECT * FROM ft WHERE ft MATCH 'abandon';
poc: yes - public, crashes the Chrome renderer through WebSQL
notes: CONTROL. The overflowed object is zBuffer, the term-reassembly buffer, grown with sqlite3_realloc64 at ext/fts3/fts3.c:1947 and written by memcpy(&zBuffer[nPrefix],zCsr,nSuffix) at :1955. The fix widens the length arithmetic to i64. A malloc-boundary check sees this write.

trigger: apply or iterate a corrupt changeset; requires -DSQLITE_ENABLE_SESSION
poc: yes - in-tree: ./sessionfuzz run test/sessionfuzz-data1.db under ASAN
notes: CONTROL. Eight bytes are read at pIn->aData[pIn->iNext] without checking pIn->nData-pIn->iNext>=8. The session module's buffers are sqlite3_malloc64 allocations (ext/session/sqlite3session.c:495, :3531), independent of any db connection arena.

bug_class: integer overflow -> out-of-bounds write (of a pointer)
trigger: corrupt FTS5 database declaring a huge nPgTombstone, then any MATCH query
notes: CONTROL. The Fts5TombstoneArray comes from sqlite3Fts5MallocZero, which is a thin wrapper over sqlite3_malloc64 (ext/fts5/fts5_buffer.c:264-267). The size computation was truncated to int, so the write leaves the malloc block.

trigger: query the zipfile() virtual table over a malformed ZIP whose Central Directory declares an uncompressed size larger than what inflate() produces
poc: yes - public crafted ZIP plus SQL that leaks a live heap pointer
notes: CONTROL, and the one to read against the 'uninitialised reads always trap' assumption: aRes = sqlite3_malloc64(nOut) (ext/misc/zipfile.c:1005) is returned in full even when inflate wrote fewer bytes, so the untouched tail of a fresh malloc block is handed back as BLOB content. Nothing about the allocation event marks those bytes; only the length fix does.

trigger: an FTS5 prefix query run inside a transaction, so the pending-term hash is non-empty
notes: CONTROL. memcmp(fts5EntryKey(pIter), pTerm, nTerm) compared nTerm bytes without checking the entry's own key length; the fix adds pIter->nKey+1>=nTerm. Fts5HashEntry records are individual sqlite3_malloc64 allocations (ext/fts5/fts5_hash.c:288), so the over-read crosses a real allocation boundary.

trigger: concat_ws(sep, ...) with an attacker-controlled separator larger than 2MB and many arguments
poc: no working public reproducer found (the referenced gist is a report, not code)
notes: CONTROL. SQLite's own CVE page states the class outright: 'a write past the end of an array obtained from malloc()'. Confirmed in source: n += (argc-1)*nSep wrapped, then z = sqlite3_malloc64(n+1) (src/func.c:1680) under-allocated. Also carries CVE-2025-29087 for the same defect.
